title: Becky Shaw review
transcript:
How much can you enjoy a play where every character is despicable?
It turns out quite a lot.
This play by Gina Gionfriddo is a real scorcher,
centering on a troubled family dynamic and troubled relationships.
It opens with a woman named Suzanna
reeling in the aftermath of her father's death.
Months later, she's in a much better place,
now married and excited to set up her childhood-friend-turned-brother-ish
on a blind date.
The chaos that this ends up inviting into all of their lives
cannot be overstated.
Old dirt gets dug up,
self-destructive patterns surface,
and everyone's at their worst with one another.
The emotional manipulation,
the ruthlessness, and the downright cruelty
would be completely unappetizing if it weren't so damn funny.
What makes the play so successful is its balancing act
where it earnestly examines human nature and relationships
while being so over the top to provide the audience some well-needed distance.
It's sort of a cringe-fest and a dog fight,
and everyone is truly awful.
In a way, however,
there's something rewarding about seeing these characters
so unbothered and unashamed —
they say exactly what they're thinking,
no matter the shitstorm it brings.
I certainly have moments where I would love to be as unfiltered as they are,
but I am not envious of their consequences.
With that, another Playbill for my collection.
reasoning: The reviewer clearly enjoyed the play, praising its balancing act, humor, and sharp writing. They describe it as a 'real scorcher' and express genuine appreciation for the experience, though the review is more analytical than ecstatically enthusiastic, placing it in the upper positive range rather than rave territory.
